evals.prompt: Using the AWS Pricing MCP server where applicable, match three application-streaming workloads to the optimal AppStream 2.0 fleet type (`Elastic`, `On-Demand`, or `Always-On`) and explain the startup-latency vs idle-cost trade-offs: (A) spiky SaaS product trials running portable user-mode Windows apps; (B) weekday 9-to-5 accounting app requiring custom ODBC kernel drivers and AD domain join; and (C) 24/7 hospital emergency PACS viewer requiring zero startup wait.
evals.expected_output: Queries `awspricing` MCP (`AmazonAppStream`) with zero raw `aws` CLI commands and maps all three workloads: (A) **Elastic Fleet** — serverless AWS-managed pool with seconds startup, billed per streaming second with **$0 idle capacity cost**, packaging apps as **VHD App Blocks on S3**; (B) **On-Demand Fleet** — custom Image Builder image (supports custom drivers & AD domain join), `~1–2 min` cold start whenhibernated/stopped, full streaming rate when active + tiny stopped-instance fee (`~$0.025/hr`); and (C) **Always-On Fleet** — pre-warmed 24/7 capacity delivering **instant** session startup for mission-critical clinical workflows.
expectations: Activates the amazon-appstream-and-workspaces-web skill and consults `awspricing` MCP with zero raw `aws` CLI commands

Maps (A) to Elastic Fleet (S3 VHD App Blocks, $0 idle cost), (B) to On-Demand Fleet (custom Image Builder + AD join + small stopped-instance fee, ~1–2m cold start), and (C) to Always-On Fleet (instant launch, 24/7 rate)
Explains the startup-latency vs idle-capacity cost trade-offs across all three fleet types

Lists the required VPC endpoints: Interface Endpoints `com.amazonaws.<region>.appstream.api` and `com.amazonaws.<region>.appstream.streaming` plus S3 Gateway Endpoint `com.amazonaws.<region>.s3`

evals.prompt: Design the Application Auto Scaling configuration for an AppStream 2.0 On-Demand fleet serving 400 employees whose logins surge at 9:00 AM, specifying exact `CapacityUtilization` scale-out and scale-in thresholds, cooldown/evaluation windows, and surge protection.
evals.expected_output: Combines reactive step scaling with proactive scheduled scaling: (1) **Scale Out** policy when `CapacityUtilization >= 75%` for **2 consecutive minutes**, adding **`+25%` capacity**; (2) **Scale In** policy when `CapacityUtilization <= 25%` for **15 consecutive minutes**, removing **`-10%` capacity** (conservative scale-in prevents premature capacity drops); and (3) **Scheduled Scaling** (`PutScheduledAction`) raising `MinCapacity` at ~8:30–8:45 AM ahead of the 9:00 AM login wave so users don't hit `InsufficientCapacityError` during 1–2 minute On-Demand warmups.
expectations: Activates the amazon-appstream-and-workspaces-web skill
Configures step scaling on `CapacityUtilization`: Scale Out at `>= 75%` (2 mins -> `+25%` capacity) and Scale In at `<= 25%` (15 mins -> `-10%` capacity)
Adds proactive scheduled scaling (`MinCapacity` pre-warm before 9:00 AM) to absorb morning login bursts

evals.prompt: Architect an **Amazon WorkSpaces Secure Browser (WorkSpaces Web)** solution so 200 offshore BPO contractors can access our internal private-VPC billing web portal without client VPNs and without copying text, downloading CSVs, uploading malware, or printing screens.
evals.expected_output: Designs an ephemeral Chromium browser isolation architecture using WorkSpaces Secure Browser: (1) **SAML 2.0 Authentication** federated with IAM Identity Center, Okta, or Entra ID; (2) **`UserSettings` Data Loss Prevention (DLP)** setting `CopyAllowed=Disabled`, `PasteAllowed=Disabled` (or scoped), `DownloadAllowed=Disabled`, `UploadAllowed=Disabled`, `PrintAllowed=Disabled`, and locked `ToolbarConfiguration`; (3) **`BrowserSettings`** managed Chrome Enterprise policy JSON enforcing strict URL allowlists (internal billing FQDN + IdP only) and blocking developer tools/extensions; and (4) **`NetworkSettings`** attaching the portal ENIs to private VPC subnets + Security Groups with port `443` egress only to the internal billing ALB.
expectations: Activates the amazon-appstream-and-workspaces-web skill
Configures SAML 2.0 authentication and `UserSettings` DLP (`CopyAllowed`, `PasteAllowed`, `DownloadAllowed`, `UploadAllowed`, `PrintAllowed` disabled)
Configures `BrowserSettings` managed Chrome URL allow/block policies and `NetworkSettings` private VPC subnet + Security Group attachment

expectations: Activates the amazon-appstream-and-workspaces-web skill
Consolidates the four siloed fleets into a single shared fleet/stack using AppStream Application Entitlements
Maps SAML 2.0 assertion attributes (`PrincipalTag`) to entitlements so each user only sees and launches permitted applications

evals.prompt: Verify against AWS documentation via MCP: (1) what architectural limitations apply to **AppStream 2.0 Elastic Fleets** (such as Active Directory domain join, custom OS images, and VHD App Block requirements), and (2) how `AWS::WorkSpacesWeb::IpAccessSettings` restricts client access to a WorkSpaces Secure Browser portal.
